{{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Cuisine of the United States|American cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Fish|Fish]] | [[Cookbook:Soups|Soups]]

'''Manhattan clam chowder''' is a [[Cookbook:Soup|soup]] traditionally made from clams, herbs, tomatoes, and other vegetables. Despite its name, it originated in Rhode Island, not Manhattan.
 
Clam chowder, in its cream-based, [[Cookbook:New England Clam Chowder|New England version]], has existed since the mid-18th Century, and no mention of any Manhattan chowder has been found that predates the 1930s.{{fact}} Many restaurants in northern Rhode Island sell both red and white chowders, while the US southern coast favors clear and white chowders. Often they are served alongside clam cakes.

According to Alton Brown, who pointed this out in the installment of his program ''Good Eats'' titled "Send In The Clams," the use of tomatoes instead of milk was initially the work of Portuguese immigrants in Rhode Island, as tomato-based stews were already a traditional part of Portuguese cuisine. New Englanders called this modified version Manhattan-style clam chowder as a pejorative because, in their snide view, calling someone a New Yorker was an insult.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Send in the Clams |url=https://www.foodnetwork.com/shows/good-eats/episodes/send-in-the-clams |access-date=2023-05-21 |website=Food Network |language=en}}</ref>

== Ingredients ==
* 15 [[Cookbook:Ounce|ounces]] (425 [[Cookbook:gram|g]]) canned [[Cookbook:Potato|potatoes]], or 2 small boiled potatoes
* 28 ounces (794 g) canned [[Cookbook:Tomato|tomatoes]] in juice, or 2 large tomatoes and tomato juice
* 6.5 ounces (184 g) canned [[Cookbook:Chopping|chopped]] [[Cookbook:Clam|clams]], minimum
* 2 stalks of [[Cookbook:Celery|celery]]

== Procedure ==
#Core the tomatoes. Remove the pale parts and the seeds; the "meat" of the tomato will be what will be used. For canned tomatoes, a strainer will be helpful.
#Chop all non-clam ingredients to match the clams in size.
#If desired add spices. Suggestions offered include [[Cookbook:Dill|dill seed]], [[Cookbook:Basil|basil]], [[Cookbook:Thyme|thyme]], [[Cookbook:Celery|celery seed]], [[Cookbook:Tarragon|tarragon]], [[Cookbook:Marjoram|marjoram]], and/or fresh [[Cookbook:Cilantro|cilantro]]. Alternatively, [[Cookbook:Oregano|oregano]] can be used in lieu of the marjoram.
#Cook the chowder, without boiling, until the celery begins to soften.

== Notes, tips, and variations ==

* A sturdy type of [[Cookbook:Fish|fish]] can be used in place of the clams; good choices include catfish, tilapia, and pollock. 
* Cooked [[Cookbook:Rice|rice]] can be substituted for the potatoes, the celery can be replaced with [[Cookbook:Spinach|spinach]] or [[Cookbook:Seaweed|seaweed]], and [[Cookbook:Lemon Juice|lemon juice]] can be added.
